pairs.subject: agent-host-experience
pairs.evidence: app/api/agents/dispatch/mint.ts:127 When Personas does not answer within the 5s bridge deadline, the dispatch door (and hire-from-need, which passes the same 502 body through to the Personas App master) reports the hire as failed even though Personas may already have queued it, and a retry mints a fresh hired_agents row and a second persona request instead of saying the outcome is unknown.

techniques.evidence: app/api/agents/dispatch/mint.ts:120 hire-from-need is shaped as a journey (route.ts:6 'ONE call from a need to a persona', closed HIRE_* codes, the scan-timeout refusal says a retry joins the in-flight scan). Step 6 is violated, though: a dispatch abandoned at its deadline is recorded and answered as failed, not unknown, so the caller's retry can double the delegation.

app/api/agents/report/[token]/route.ts:20 kp delegates long-running work to a Personas peer and treats its reports as untrusted. Each hire has its own token as the grant, the body is capped, rate-limited and shape-parsed, and lifecycle claims go through a CAS transition that refuses illegal moves.

app/api/companion/[id]/message/route.ts:24 The product's own agent (the companion) is a single request/response per turn that returns the stored turn list. Its proposals are filed and resolved on a separate door, so there is no multi-surface live run and the technique's 'when not to use' applies.

app/api/companion/[id]/message/route.ts:122 Companion blocks are an in-app vocabulary that only kp's own dock renders. No outside host or interop format consumes them (no MCP/tool server in the repo), so nothing is projected.

pairs.registryProposal: The subject assumes the outside agent reaches the product through a tool protocol. Here an outside agent (Personas App master) reaches a journey-shaped HTTP door (hire-from-need) that is gated by a shared machine token, and the product also delegates to that same peer. The techniques could say explicitly whether a plain HTTP 'machine door' for a known peer falls under journey-shaped-tool-surface.

pairs.subject: agent-host-experience
pairs.evidence: app/features/library/jobs/JobsAgentFitTab.tsx:16 These are panels inside kp's own front end, where consent is already home (depth-handoff's own exclusion). A search of app/features/library/jobs for tool-protocol and view-resource vocabulary found no outward tool, view or stream surface, so the subject's outside-tier precondition does not hold.

declined.subject: agent-host-experience
declined.reason: A Playwright suite (including the app-master-hire spec against a mock Personas bridge) exercises the agent-hire surfaces but does not itself realize any of this subject's techniques. Any verdict would repeat the agents-api judgement on test files.
